We didn't queer the institution of marriage: It straightened us (The Guardian)

I never understood the push for marriage "rights" State sponsored marriage is rooted in anti miscegentaion. The push all along should have been to get the state out of marriage and let people define their own relationships.

There's this book by Friedrich Engels that outlines the origins of the institution of marriage. Going back to the advent of agriculture and private property - what happens when you've claimed some land as your own and raised crops on it your whole life? Well, you die, eventually. And you want to make sure that the person benefiting from your property after you die is your own genetic descendant.

So, you create this other institution that operates alongside the institution of private property. It's called marriage, and it designates a woman as your property, your chattel. You have exclusive rights to the use of her reproductive organs. This guarantees that any child she bears will share your genetic material.

This is also where the old fear of adultery and women who choose multiple sexual partners originates. Women who refused to only have sex with one man became a direct threat to the concept of private property. A woman whose sexuality is not controlled by one man can bear the child of anyone, paternity is unknowable, and the child cannot inherit property (a "bastard" or "illegitimate child").

So, as a threat to private property, these women faced not only prejudice and disdain, but severe punishments. Look to the koran and the old testament, and you will see what an extreme threat to a society based on private property these women were seen as. For the crime of refusing to be owned by one man, or the crime of bearing a child of questionable paternity, women were faced with death by some of the most barbaric methods.

Marriage is an institution rooted in misogyny, slavery, heterosexual supremacy, and private property. I don't see it as something queer people should be buying into, or something we should be fighting for the right to participate in.
